title: Former MLB GM says Red Sox had ‘biggest overpay’ before trade deadline
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Jim Bowden labeled Boston's trade for Curtis Mead as MLB's 'biggest overpay' before the deadline.
The Red Sox traded pitcher Connelly Early to acquire Curtis Mead from the Nationals.
Curtis Mead injured his wrist in his first game, sidelining him for six to eight weeks.

title: Brockton mayor suing state, says 2025 crash involving State Trooper left him disabled
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Brockton Mayor Moises Rodrigues filed a lawsuit against Massachusetts following a 2025 crash with a State Trooper.
The crash allegedly left Rodrigues with over $32,000 in medical bills and partially disabled, according to the lawsuit.
The State Police report cited Trooper Augustine Moore's inattention as a factor, and Rodrigues seeks a jury trial.

title: Grant Williams explains relationship dynamic between Jayson Tatum, Jaylen Brown
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Grant Williams clarifies that Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown had a respectful relationship despite not being close off-court.
Tatum and Brown had a successful nine-year tenure with the Celtics, including an NBA Championship win in 2024.
Jayson Tatum denies any past animosity, emphasizing media attempts to create conflict during their time together.

title: Cyclospora cases climb to 147 in Mass., but officials say season remains within historical range
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Massachusetts reports 147 cyclospora cases from May 1 to Aug. 1, linked to contaminated iceberg lettuce.
DPH says Massachusetts' cyclospora cases are higher than usual but within historical range of 23 to 211 annually.
The FDA ties recalled iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms to the cyclosporiasis outbreak; no deaths reported in Massachusetts.

title: Tow truck driver charged with motor vehicle homicide, police say he hit ‘highly visible’ pedestrian in Worcester
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Andrew Peperato, 52, charged with motor vehicle homicide for killing pedestrian Van Thi Khanh Doan in Worcester.
Peperato was allegedly using his cellphone when his truck hit Doan in a crosswalk on June 10.
Peperato faces multiple charges, including negligent operation and improper turning, with arraignment set for September 17.

title: Does Christian Gonzalez’ contract stalemate make Drake Maye think about his own Patriots future?
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Christian Gonzalez's contract stalemate with New England Patriots continues, despite an offer to become highest-paid cornerback.
Patriots QB Drake Maye, eligible for a contract extension after 2026, remains focused on the upcoming season.
Maye, a potential contender for a high-paying deal, admires Gonzalez's participation in training camp amid contract talks.

title: 18-year-old uses ‘grit and determination’ to help with own rescue from Mount Washington
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Andrew Nelson, 18, crawled partway to meet rescuers after injuring his leg on Mount Washington.
Nelson was injured on Tuckerman Ravine Trail, about half a mile from the summit, with eight friends.
Rescuers splinted Nelson's leg and carried him to the summit; he declined hospital transport.

title: Woman sues Court TV over release of her name in Irish firefighter rape case
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: A woman is suing Court TV for $2.8 million, alleging her identity was disclosed in a rape case broadcast.
The lawsuit claims the woman's name was shown during an Irish firefighter's 2025 retrial for rape in Boston.
Court TV's error reportedly led to online harassment, worsening the woman's anxiety and necessitating further therapy.

title: Healey signs sweeping law to restrict ICE
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Gov. Maura Healey signed the Protect Act in Chelsea, limiting ICE operations in schools, hospitals, and courthouses.
The Protect Act prohibits warrantless immigration arrests and allows parents to arrange guardianship if deported.
The law grants residents a civil rights claim against government officials, including ICE, for constitutional rights violations.

title: Here’s how Mass. hospitals fared in the latest U.S. News rankings
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Brigham and Women's and Massachusetts General hospitals ranked top in Massachusetts and made the national honor roll.
Dana-Farber Brigham Cancer Center ranked third nationwide for cancer care in U.S. News rankings.
Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center was ranked third in Massachusetts, followed by Lahey Clinic and Boston Medical Center.
